_about: Neutral display data layered on Robertson's sections (src/data/harmony.json). t = title (describes what the texts narrate); p = place key, or a per-gospel map when the gospels name different places; pb = 'implied' when the place is inferred from context rather than named; from = per gospel [place key, reference, quoted words] where the text has Jesus set out from somewhere other than the last place on the route, so the route line keeps the journey's shape; toward = per gospel [place key, reference, quoted words] where the text has Jesus making for a place he hasn't reached yet, shown on the map as a heading. light: per gospel [state, reference, quoted words, 'stated' | 'implied'], only where the text states a time or the inference is widely agreed.

mapStart._about: The map shows Jesus from this section on: Mary visits Elizabeth (Lk 1:39–45), the first scene with him present, carried by Mary. Before it there is no marker, no route and no likely area.

birth._about: Jesus is born in this section (Lk 2:6–7). From here on, in scenes he isn't in, his resting marker keeps a little of its glow and of his light on the land (until his death; see death).

moves._about: Sections shown somewhere other than where Robertson places them: the reader puts each one after the section given, and its kicker says so (with this note). `after` must be a section; `words` are quoted from `ref` and checked by validate. The order flags still compare each gospel with its own order.

s141.note: Robertson (§141) places this where Matthew and Mark tell it, after the plot “two days” before the Passover (Mk 14:1). Many harmonies place it here instead, by John’s date: “Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany” and “they hosted a dinner for Jesus there” (Jn 12:1–2).

jesusAbsent._about: Sections where Jesus is not in the scene. The map's route line tracks only his own movements, so these get a plain scene marker and no line. Mary's visit and song (s6, s7) count as present: she is carrying him and stays with Elizabeth until Lk 1:56; John's birth (s8) follows her return home.

areas._about: Radius in km for places shown as areas rather than points. The wilderness is the Judaean Desert between Bethany and Jericho, clear of the Dead Sea; Beyond the Jordan is Perea, east of the river.

mountains._about: Sections whose text places Jesus on, near or going up a mountain or hill (figurative uses, quotations and parables left out). The words are checked against the BSB. While one is on screen, the map shows the named peaks within 15 km of the place or area shown, with their contours.

mountainPeaks._about: Mountain sections whose mountain is given here (Wikidata IDs from peaks), shown in place of the named peaks nearest where Jesus is. 'named': the text names it (the Mount of Olives), so no other peak is offered. 'candidates': the text doesn't name it, so the map card says these are candidates; for the transfiguration's 'high mountain', Mount Hermon, near Caesarea Philippi where the preceding scenes are set, Meron, the highest in Galilee, or Mount Tabor, the traditional site (the user's choice).

peaks._about: Named peaks the map can show in mountain sections, by Wikidata ID (names, positions and Wikipedia articles from Wikidata, CC0). Each value is [radius in km of the contour window, search radius in km for the summit]. The marker moves to the highest point of the terrain tiles (SRTM) within the search radius; 0 keeps Wikidata's position, for sites that aren't summits (a church on a hillside, a city hill).

dates._about: Estimated dates as decimal years in astronomical numbering (year 0 = 1 BC, so -3.6 is in 5 BC). Two common reckonings, crucifixion in AD 30 or AD 33. Rows between anchors are interpolated by order; these are estimates for laying out the timeline, not claims about exact dates.
anchors: before the death of Herod the Great in 4 BC (Mt 2:1, 19)
the years that follow in Nazareth (Lk 2:51–52)
“the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius” (Lk 3:1), counted from AD 12 or AD 14
Friday 7 April AD 30 or Friday 3 April AD 33
